item.title: Making Lin Yue Move
item.description: After building Lin Yue, the next challenge was making her move. A look at Kimodo motion references, a motor-inspired rig, procedural pose scripts, and the shoes and guards that had to move with her.

item.title: From Voxels to Lin Yue
item.description: What began as an experiment in reverse engineering a GLB became a journey through voxel scanning, mesh wrapping, procedural geometry and signed distance fields. Follow my attempts to build Lin Yue for The Jade Crypt, from mannequin-derived scans and awkward early prototypes to an original rigged character with procedural animations—and plenty of challenges still to solve.

item.title: Reverse Engineering My Own Game
item.description: How much of a shipped Godot game can someone recover? I put my own game, The Jade Crypt, to the test using REA’s AI-assisted reverse-engineering toolkit and GDRE Tools. While REA encountered a binary format boundary, GDRE recovered all 66 GDScript files in just six seconds, with no meaningful logic differences detected. This experiment explores what survives decompilation, what gets lost, and how Godot developers can make their released games harder to reverse engineer through export filtering, encryption, and obfuscation.

item.title: Building The Jade Crypt
item.description: A behind-the-scenes look at building The Jade Crypt, a 2.5D cinematic Wuxia platformer in Godot 4. The post explores the evolution from procedural character animation to skeletal locomotion, a modular headless validation engine, ASCII-driven level design, and an AI-assisted toolchain for 3D assets, cinematics, and audio.
